lines.text: Clip this on your finger, and in seconds it knows how much oxygen is in your blood, without a single needle. How?
One side shines two colors through your finger: red light and invisible infrared. A sensor on the other side measures what gets through.
Blood rich in oxygen soaks up more infrared. Blood low in oxygen soaks up more red.
So the ratio of red to infrared tells the device how saturated your blood is.
But your finger is also skin, bone and veins. The trick is your heartbeat.
Each beat pushes a little extra arterial blood in, so the device only looks at the part of the signal that pulses.
That's also why movement, cold fingers, or poor circulation can make readings less reliable.
